description: Committee recommends full cost recovery for EV charging.
User fees will be over $5 per hour, starting soon.
Also directs exploring private sector partnerships for charging.

chips.text: Defeated
2 for, 4 against
Mayor Block stated it is time to 'take the training wheels off' for EV charging subsidies.
Administration recommended a $3 per hour fee, but committee chose full cost recovery.
EV users appreciated the free pilot, but non-EV users complained about public funding.
Councillor Davies opposed subsidies, stating taxpayers should not fund private vehicle choices.
Public charging removes a key barrier for multi-unit residents without home options.
The pilot reduced an estimated 30 tons of greenhouse gases.
Administration will monitor EV charging station usage and report back in one year.

description: City will offer optional program for customers to offset electricity emissions.

This replaces the old Green Power program.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Staff noted the old program was oversubscribed but now has only 18 customers.
NULIFE GreenTech Inc. revenues would drop 20% without the program.
Mayor Block questioned why renewable energy costs more, disputing staff's explanation.
NULIFE GreenTech Inc. strongly urged adoption, citing economic benefits and local job creation.
Program helps the city meet its net zero GHG emissions target.
Mayor Block wants revenues to fund future renewable energy projects.
